title: Mary-Dell Chilton Dies at 87; Helped Create First Genetically Modified Plant
partialText: In 1982, she led the research team that figured out how to genetically alter plants, a discovery that would eventually transform global agriculture.

title: White House Faces Stiff Pushback on Subjecting Grants to Political Review
partialText: Academics, city leaders and congressional lawmakers number among the thousands to urge the Trump administration to reconsider a plan to assert more control over grants.

title: Americans Are Spending, and Not Just on Necessities
partialText: Lower gas prices have been a relief for households struggling with higher living costs. But now they are creeping higher again.

title: Maker of Drone Boats Used in Iran War Will Open New Texas Shipyard
partialText: Saronic Technologies will make naval and commercial vessels at the facility. The company’s naval drone helped rescue the crew of a downed Apache helicopter last month.

title: Strait of Hormuz Tanker Traffic Erodes Further as Oil Prices Rise
partialText: Very few ships passed through the waterway on the first full day of the U.S. naval blockade of Iran.

title: Anthropic Inches Toward a Mega-I.P.O.
partialText: The artificial intelligence lab is said to have taken more steps that are consistent with a company aiming to go public in the fall.

title: Google Ordered to Give A.I. Rivals More Access on Android Smartphones
partialText: The decision by European Union regulators is a response to fears that Google will use its vast Android user base to gain an edge in A.I.

title: U.K. Nationalizes British Steel, Its Last Major Steel Mill
partialText: The government first intervened in British Steel last year to prevent its then-owner, the Chinese company Jingye Group, from shutting it down. No private sector buyers came forward.

title: TSMC Adds $100 Billion to Its U.S. Spending Plan
partialText: The pledge from the Taiwanese chip-making giant brought the total commitment to its fast-growing operations in Arizona to $265 billion.

title: Diesel Prices Hit $5 a Gallon Again, Up 33% Since Start of Iran War
partialText: U.S. diesel prices first surpassed $5 a gallon in March. Renewed fighting in the Persian Gulf and reduced refinery capacity are pushing up prices again.

title: India Is Moving Fast to Build A.I. Data Centers. A Coastal City May Pay the Price.
partialText: With India lagging in the technology, officials are embracing giant data centers. But critics say the megaprojects will use up energy and water, without providing long-term jobs.

title: The Quest for ‘Technological Sovereignty’ in Europe (and Why It’s So Hard)
partialText: France and Germany want to quit relying on America and China for key technology like artificial intelligence, but they’re having to choose where to do it.

title: Trump Administration to Impose New Tariffs on Brazil
partialText: The United States accused the country of unfair trade practices. The tariff will replace ones that the Supreme Court struck down.

title: New York Times Files Motion to Quash Subpoenas of Its Journalists
partialText: The Justice Department is seeking to compel grand jury testimony as part of an investigation into Times reporting on the president’s new Air Force One jet.

title: NextEra and Dominion File to Form a Huge Power Company
partialText: They asked regulators in three states and at a federal agency to approve a deal that would create a combined company with 10 million customers across the Southeast.

title: PayPal Receives $53 Billion Takeover Offer Involving Stripe
partialText: PayPal, which owns Venmo, is the target of what one group of analysts described as a “lowball” offer from Stripe, another payment processor, and Advent, a private equity firm.

title: United Airlines Will Soon Let You Take Over the Middle Seat, for a Price
partialText: The option, set to go on sale on some flights later this year, will feature a shared table in the middle seat. The move may actually save the airline money.

title: Senators Grill Justice Dept. Officials on New York Times Subpoenas
partialText: Democrats questioned the acting attorney general, Todd Blanche, and a U.S. attorney about subpoenas issued to Times journalists who reported on security concerns with the president’s new plane.

title: Treasury to Begin Minting $1 Gold Trump Coin Featuring President’s Face
partialText: Critics question whether the coins are legal and argue that President Trump is using the currency to celebrate himself.

title: SpaceX Briefly Falls Below I.P.O. Price of $135
partialText: After soaring in its stock market debut, the shares of Elon Musk’s rocket and A.I. company have been rocky.

title: War Risk for Businesses Will Mean Higher Prices No Matter What Happens
partialText: Doing business in a more dangerous and unpredictable world will cost more, pushing up the price of everything from food to electronics.

title: Goldman’s Former Top Lawyer Calls Epstein a ‘Masterful Liar’
partialText: Kathryn Ruemmler, the former general counsel of Goldman Sachs, testified on Wednesday in a closed-door congressional hearing investigating Jeffery Epstein.

title: IBM’s Stock Crash Reignites Fears of A.I. Disruption in Software Sector
partialText: The company tumbled sharply after previewing quarterly results that were disappointing. It’s not good news for software and tech consulting companies.

title: Oil Prices Tick Higher as U.S. Reinstates Iran Blockade
partialText: The United States reinstated its blockade on Iranian ports in the Strait of Hormuz and shipping slowed to a crawl amid the renewed warfare in the critical waterway.

title: A Year After DOGE Cuts, Social Security Is Trying to Stabilize
partialText: The agency has been quietly hiring workers again, and its leadership is focused on improving technology to ease workloads left by the departure of about 7,800 staff members.

title: The American E.V. Has Been Crushed. Will It Take the U.S. Auto Industry With It?
partialText: The largest U.S. automakers have backed away from electric vehicles, even as global sales are booming. The decision may make them obsolete.

title: Twitter Turns 20: Two Decades of Memes, Movements and Hot Takes
partialText: The first tweets from the public appeared on July 15, 2006, several months after a soft launch. It was rebranded as X after being acquired by Elon Musk.

title: What Trump’s New Iran Blockade Could Mean for Oil Prices
partialText: The first blockade in April choked off Iranian exports without causing a lasting price surge. Now global oil reserves are lower, and ships face heightened risks.

title: CXMT, China’s Chip Champion, to Raise Billions in Race for A.I. Control
partialText: CXMT, a linchpin in China’s drive to develop homegrown artificial intelligence technology, is aiming to raise nearly $10 billion in a blockbuster public offering in Shanghai.

title: China’s Economy Grows at Slowest Pace in Years
partialText: Economic growth of 4.3 percent in the second quarter, versus the same period last year, reflected a broad slump outside of the country’s export-oriented manufacturing might.

title: Tech Investors and Longevity Influencers Back Neko Health’s Mega Round
partialText: The health tech start-up co-founded by Spotify’s Daniel Ek is worth billions more after a new $700 million funding round.

title: Data Centers to Add Billions in Power Costs in 13 States
partialText: A power auction conducted by a giant grid operator is expected to add $6.3 billion in additional charges to consumers and businesses because of electricity needs of data centers.

title: Public Health Groups Sue F.D.A. Over Flavored E-Cigarette Policy
partialText: Executives unhappy with the agency donated and lobbied President Trump directly. Major companies have already begun to prepare and ship new products.

title: Top Tax Official to Leave Trump Administration
partialText: Ken Kies, who held two top jobs at the Treasury Department and the I.R.S., is leaving the government.

title: Trump Flip-Flops on Strait of Hormuz, Creating New Risks for Global Economy
partialText: The president now wants Gulf nations to invest in the U.S. in exchange for safe passage. Shipping industry experts worry other nations will follow that lead.

title: Chipotle Is Bringing Its Mexican-Inspired Fast Food to Monterrey, Mexico
partialText: The California-based restaurant chain is opening its first location south of the U.S.-Mexico border this week, bringing its bowls and burritos to Monterrey.

title: Leonard Abramson, Health Care Innovator and Philanthropist, Dies at 93
partialText: He created U.S. Healthcare, one of the first H.M.O.s, and used his great wealth from the sale of the company for causes like advancing cancer research.

title: Trump Paid $2 Million by South Korean Company Facing Trade Investigation
partialText: The payment illustrates the minefield Mr. Trump has created by maintaining personal financial ties with foreign businesses while he is in office.

title: Warren Buffet Declines to Donate to Gates Foundation Amid Epstein Revelations
partialText: The decision by the Berkshire Hathaway founder comes in the wake of Epstein revelations that have troubled the Gates Foundation.

title: T. Rex Fossil Sells for $50.1 Million, Putting the King Back On Top
partialText: In a booming fossil market, the T. rex had been dethroned by a stegosaurus. No longer.

title: White House Cheers Inflation Data While Iran War Sparks New Price Surge
partialText: The news of an improvement in consumer prices in June came as the U.S. and Iran escalated attacks, risking a return to high energy prices.

title: What to know about the Fed chairman’s testimony.
The Fed’s new chairman is asking for advice.
partialText: Five new task forces are focused on topics that Kevin M. Warsh, the chairman of the Federal Reserve, has said are “central to the broad conduct of monetary policy.”

title: Warsh Reiterates Fed’s Pledge to Get Inflation Down but Doesn’t Specify How
partialText: Kevin M. Warsh, in his first testimony to Congress as chairman of the Federal Reserve, did not shed light on whether he supported higher interest rates to tame price pressures.

title: Paramount vs. the States
partialText: An effort to block the media giant’s planned takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery underscores how states are taking a more active role in antitrust regulation.

title: Chai Discovery, an A.I. Drug Start-Up, Raises $400 Million
partialText: The fund-raising values the company at $3.8 billion and underscores investor interest in using artificial intelligence to tackle problems like drug discovery.

title: Big Banks Smash Earnings Records, but ‘Tectonic’ Risks Loom
partialText: The quarterly results reflect the dichotomy between geopolitical uncertainty and the stable American economy.

title: Inflation Slowed During Pause in War With Iran
partialText: The Consumer Price Index fell to a 3.5 percent annual increase in June, and prices marked their biggest drop from a month earlier since 2020.

title: China Purges Top Official Over Corruption and Sex Charges
partialText: Ma Xingrui is the third member of the Politburo to be purged since 2022. He once led the Xinjiang region and was previously head of China’s space program.

title: U.S. Workers Are More Productive Than Ever. A.I. Isn’t the Key.
partialText: Companies have been getting more out of employees for several years. Tight labor markets, digitization and remote work are among the reasons.
